threads.thread_goal: Lock capsule concept, theme, and target customer before detailed design.

messages.text: Hey team, I've started pulling together the initial concept for the capsule collection. I've dropped a first pass of the moodboard into A1. The working theme is 'Urban Bloom' - thinking about the intersection of nature and industrial cityscapes. Let me know your thoughts. This is the first step for T1.

Thanks for starting this. I like the 'Urban Bloom' concept. Looking at A1, some of those textures look complex. We should keep our supplier list in mind, especially for the more technical fabrics. Do we have a price point in mind? That will influence our material choices heavily.
Love the direction! I can already see some cool graphic treatments. Maybe some distorted floral photography mixed with clean, sans-serif type? I can mock something up really quick if that helps.

Good point on the fabrics. I've already cross-checked the key textures with our top 3 suppliers and they seem to have stock. For positioning, I was thinking premium-accessible, similar to our last drop. Target customer would be the 25-35 creative professional. I'll add a persona slide to A1.
Yeah that sounds cool. Or what about like a graffiti-style flower? Something really bright and pop.

Interesting idea. Let's keep the graphic exploration broad for now. The main goal is to lock the core theme. I think the 'distorted floral' idea from @133615 feels a bit closer to the moodboard's tone. Let's not get too far into execution on the graphics just yet.
Catching up on this. The 'Urban Bloom' concept is strong and has legs. The contrast is compelling. I agree with the premium-accessible positioning. Let's formalize these points.
Decision: The final capsule theme is 'Urban Bloom', focusing on the contrast between natural forms and industrial textures. (D1)
Decision: The target customer is the 25-35 year old creative professional, with a premium-accessible price point. (D2). I've updated the notes in A1 to reflect this. Great start everyone.

threads.thread_goal: Review and refine garment sketches, silhouettes, and hero looks.

messages.text: Morning all, as promised, I've uploaded 12 initial garment sketches to the project folder. This is for T2. I've tried to offer a range of silhouettes, from more structured outerwear to softer jersey pieces. Let me know which ones are resonating.

These look great. Sketch-07, the one with the asymmetric zip, is interesting but might be tricky for production on our timeline. The seam work is complex. Sketch-02 and Sketch-05 look very feasible and fit the theme well.

Wow, these are awesome! I immediately love Sketch-01 (the jacket), Sketch-04 (the wide-leg pant), Sketch-09 (the dress), and Sketch-11 (the printed tee). I think those four would be amazing hero looks for marketing.
I like them. What is a silhouette?

It's the overall shape or outline of the garment. For example, a wide-leg pant vs a skinny pant have very different silhouettes. @147978 good flag on Sketch-07, we can simplify the construction if we decide to move forward with it. Thanks for the feedback so far!
Just reviewed the sketches. Strong work. There's a clear point of view. Based on the feedback and theme, I suggest we move forward with a shortlist.
Let's lock in the following 8 SKUs: Sketch-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09, 10, and 11. This gives us a good mix of tops, bottoms, and an outerwear piece. (D3)

And for the 4 hero looks for 3D prototyping (T4), I agree with @133615's suggestions: Sketch-01 (jacket), Sketch-04 (pant), Sketch-09 (dress), and Sketch-11 (tee). These will give us the most marketing impact. I'll create the folder for them in A5. (D4)

threads.thread_goal: Align on visual identity, logo lockups, and graphic direction.

messages.text:
Hi team, I've put together three potential visual identity directions for the capsule, as part of T5. They are in the shared drive. 
- Direction A: 'Glitch Garden' - uses distorted florals and a clean, techy font.
- Direction B: 'Concrete Petals' - high-contrast B&W photography with a serif font.
- Direction C: 'Neon Growth' - uses bright color overlays and a bold, expressive script font.

Let me know which one you're leaning towards!
Direction C is sick! The neon is really eye-catching.

Thanks for putting these together so quickly. My vote is for Direction A. 'Glitch Garden' feels like the most direct translation of our 'Urban Bloom' theme. The tension between the organic and digital elements is perfect. Direction C might be a bit too loud for the subtlety of the garments.
I also lean towards Direction A. The logo lockup proposed there looks clean and versatile. How would it scale down for a garment label or a hangtag? We need to make sure it's legible at small sizes.
Good question! I tested the lockup from Direction A at smaller sizes and it holds up well. I can add those examples to the presentation.
Okay, the consensus seems clear. Direction A, 'Glitch Garden', is the strongest and most aligned with the capsule concept.
Decision: We are moving forward with visual identity Direction A, 'Glitch Garden'. (D5)
Let's also approve the primary logo lockup and the core color palette from that direction. @133615 please document these in the Visual Identity Guidelines A3. (D6)

threads.thread_goal: Finalize production specs, colorways, and fabric choices.

messages.text: Hi all, I've completed the first draft of the technical drawings for the 8 selected SKUs (T3). I've also populated the SKU and Colorway Matrix in A2 with proposed fabric and color options based on our supplier list. Everything is linked in the main project folder. Please review, especially the fabric choices for T11.

This is great, thanks for pulling it all together. I'm looking at A2 now. The Japanese denim for the jacket (Sketch-01) is perfect. However, the ribbed knit for Sketch-09 shows low stock on the supplier portal. I'd suggest we use the Tencel blend we used last season as a backup option, it has a similar drape and is fully in stock.
Excellent catch. The Tencel blend is a solid alternative. I'll update the matrix in A2 to list that as the primary choice. Any other flags?
Can you share the final hex codes from the color palette once they are locked? I'll need them for the marketing assets.
Team, I've reviewed the specs and the updated color/fabric matrix in A2. Everything looks solid. The Tencel swap is a smart move.
Let's make it official. Decision: The final colorways and fabric combinations as documented in A2 (v2.0) are approved. (D7)
@147978 please consolidate everything into the final folder, run it against the checklist in A4, and we can consider the spec pack signed off for handoff (T8). (D8)

threads.thread_goal: Align on e-commerce and social launch assets and timelines.

messages.text: Hey everyone, here are some draft layouts for the e-commerce pages (T7) and a few concepts for the social media teasers (T9). The files are in the marketing folder. The ideas are mostly static images for now.

Thanks for getting this started! Building on your concepts, what if we did a short motion graphic for the teaser? We could reveal the 'glitch floral' pattern over a silhouette of one of the hero pieces. I can work up a quick storyboard.

Good start. For the e-commerce layouts, let's make sure we have a template that includes at least one detail shot and one shot showing the garment's texture. Also, let's definitely use the 3D turntable clips from A5 for the social launch. They are perfect for showing off the hero looks.
Ok, I can add placeholders for those shots in the templates. The 3D clips are a good idea.
Great discussion. It sounds like we have a clear path forward for the assets.
Decision: We'll confirm the e-commerce image style and layout templates as drafted by @86155, with the addition of dedicated texture/detail shots. Please update this in A6. (D9)

Decision: For social, we'll proceed with a 3-part teaser sequence: 1) The motion graphic concept from @133615, 2) A carousel post with 3D turntable clips, 3) A final grid post revealing the full collection. Let's document this in A7. (D10)

Sounds great. I'll get started on the motion graphic storyboard. I'll also take the lead on pulling together the final capsule overview deck for A8, since I have all the visual assets handy. That's the last piece for T12.
